extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and the public interested in current events (1940)
extracted.subtask_description: An Associated Press newspaper dispatch reporting battlefield developments, political reactions, government organization for national defense, and related policy proposals during the May 1940 European campaign. Focused on conveying facts, official statements, and commentary to a broad readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of Edward R. Stettinius, Jr.
rubrics_metrics.description: Will handle materials up to the point where they are ready for conversion into finished articles. For instance, he will have supervision over the entire machinery conversion of the ore into steel billets, and its manufacture into unfinished steel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Header: WASHINGTON, MAY 28 — HERE ARE THE DUTIES OF THE SEVEN MEMBERS ... AS PRESIDENT ROOSEVELT OUTLINED THEM.) This item describes responsibility for early-stage material control and industrial-materials supervision for national defense production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of William S. Knudsen
rubrics_metrics.description: Will pick up from there and look after the actual production of a tank and its engine, or an airplane and its engine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible for overseeing actual finished-article production (assembly/production of weapons and vehicles) following the materials/conversion phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of Sidney Hillman
rubrics_metrics.description: Will look after work in plants, apprenticeships, instruction of CCC boys in non-combatant work, training of aviation ground crews, and development of radiomen, communications people and even cooks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers workforce training, plant labor issues, apprenticeship programs, and development of essential non-combatant technical personnel for defense (including logistics roles such as cooks). Note President’s comment that mentioning 'cooks' sounded silly but was important due to shortages for the Army and Navy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of Chester C. Davis
rubrics_metrics.description: Will work on problems connected with agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charged with addressing agricultural issues related to the national defense program (food production/supply considerations for wartime needs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of Ralph Budd
rubrics_metrics.description: His first major task will be setting up machinery that would be necessary if a transportation jam developed. (However the President stressed that the railroads are in excellent shape to handle any volume of business.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on transport/railroad contingency planning and setting up systems to avoid or manage transportation bottlenecks during mobilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of Leon Henderson
rubrics_metrics.description: Will have to establish a sort of statistical office to keep in touch with trends on consumption and to get ore from deposits, transporting it to steel plants, ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and run statistical/monitoring systems for material supply chains (consumption trends, ore extraction and transport to plants) to inform defense production planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of the Seventh Member (unnamed/collective context)
rubrics_metrics.description: The article frames a seven-member special national defense commission made up of seven prominent individuals who will participate in supervision of the billion-dollar defense program; duties are allocated among the named members as outlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual header: President Roosevelt outlined duties for seven members (chairman Edward R. Stettinius Jr. and others) to cover material handling, production oversight, labor/training, agriculture, transportation contingency machinery, and statistical monitoring for national defense mobilization.
